newsitem.title: FRANCE: France cheered by record 1996 trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: France cheered by record 1996 trade surplus.

text.p: France reported a record 1996 trade surplus of 122 billion francs ($22 billion) Tuesday, claimed the surge as more proof of an economic upturn and predicted another boost for the economy from exports this year.
"This trade surplus is a precursor to economic upturn," Yves Galland, junior minister for foreign trade, told a news conference, adding that the surplus was clearly "structural."
Galland said exports rose 4 percent in 1996 while imports increased by only 2.2 percent.

News of the surplus and the bullish 1997 outlook followed other positive soundings for the economy, such as a survey showing markedly greater optimism among industrialists on the prospects for increased production, as well as a surprise drop in unemployment in December.

A key measure of economic performance comes Wednesday, however, with the release of data on consumer spending on manufactured products. Economists polled by Reuters predict a rise of 0.8 percent, helped in part by January discount sales.

France's official forecast is for economic growth of 2.3 percent this year after an estimated 1.3 percent rise in 1996, but the government is already talking of growth exceeding its initial estimates for 1997.
